S1_owned_group: Reserve private group identity at actual setsid launch: generation, leader PID/start token, PGID, SID and uid. Verify PGID=SID=leader PID and separation from the supervisor group before recording ownership. Keep this identity after leader exit; do not treat Popen.poll/wait as group death.

Observe the complete /proc process set for live members of the exact reserved PGID and SID, retaining PID/start tokens and uid. Zombies are stopped execution, not live survivors. Revalidate observations around signalling. A vanished individual member is a normal race; inaccessible/inconsistent membership or identity ambiguity is unknown, never an empty proven group. Never match executable names or widen to another PGID/SID.

Use a monotonic group-stop state machine: TERM the proven group, continue observing despite leader exit, KILL remaining proven group members by group signal no later than0.25s after TERM, and observe the group for at most1.0s after escalation. No blocking Popen.wait and no early already-dead-leader success. Reap the Popen leader separately.

Publish terminated/image_consistent=false and ended=true only after a complete trusted observation establishes no live member in the owned group. Signal delivery, ESRCH on one PID, or leader death alone cannot clear busy. On observation failure retain unknown/outstanding/quarantine and refuse reconstruction; no signals after a group has been established dead or ownership becomes ambiguous.
S2_deadline_service: Keep the single supervisor as the only lifecycle/publication owner. Convert accepted client sockets to nonblocking bounded buffers and selector read/write states. Accept never calls receive_line synchronously; response handling never calls blocking sendall. Retain FRAME_LIMIT, finite per-client CONTROL_SECONDS deadlines, closed-envelope validation and disconnected-client semantics.

Move source_provenance, Git subprocess waits, manifest/committed-body reads and full historical reconciliation into bounded read-only verification jobs outside selector callbacks. A forked private helper can call the existing functions and return only a bounded result over a selector-managed pipe; it inherits no runtime control writer/server ownership. No new public CLI/schema or arbitrary executable selection is introduced. The helper has a separate proven process group and finite cleanup; its wait/termination must itself be asynchronous.

Correlate each read-only job with a private state version and exact session/generation/owner/lease/outstanding reference/contract-step-attempt snapshot plus input digests. Before applying a successful result, recheck those identities and live attempt. If runtime completion/cancellation, transfer, reconstruction or a file disagreement invalidated the snapshot, refuse/revalidate; late helper output cannot publish handoff, execute work or free the lane. Helpers never publish session/operation records.

Queue execute/cancel frames on a nonblocking runtime stdin with bounded storage and selector writes; eliminate buffered write/flush blocking. Preserve durable running and cancel_requested(false) publication before queueing their respective frames. Arm min(1,operation timeout including0) from durable cancellation publication before any request verification, socket send, pipe write or helper cleanup.

At each event-loop turn service due cancellation/group-stop phases before client/provenance work, between bounded I/O batches and after every callback. Select timeout is the minimum of cancellation, TERM/KILL/death observation, client, poll and verification-job deadlines. Process bounded chunks rather than draining an attacker-controlled ready descriptor indefinitely.

Bounded local atomic record publication remains ordered and preserves crash-disagreement checks. No project-selected file/Git traversal, entire-history walk, blocking socket/pipe operation, child wait or sleep remains on an armed-deadline callback. If qualification finds a retained callback can exceed the nearest deadline, this architecture is incomplete and must return for assessment rather than declaring the selector timeout sufficient.

helper_boundary_A1: Before any verification, the forked helper establishes its own session/group and closes every inherited descriptor except an explicit allowlist: its serialized read-only job-input endpoint, its sole bounded result-writer endpoint, any specifically enumerated read-only input descriptors, and standard streams deliberately rebound to /dev/null. No inherited descriptor is retained merely because helper code does not use it.

Explicitly close supervisor.lock/flock, server listener, every accepted/waiting client socket, runtime stdin/stdout/stderr and private protocol endpoints, parent result readers, sibling-job endpoints, startup/response pipes, selector descriptor and all other parent-only handles. Result/input endpoints are private to this job; exec inheritance is disabled so Git descendants cannot retain them. The helper cannot preserve a supervisor lock, keep a client/control endpoint open, signal through the runtime writer, or publish session/operation records.

Use a bounded initial handshake after descriptor isolation and setsid, reporting PID/start token/PGID/SID/uid and job nonce. The supervisor proves this separately owned group before authorizing verification. Git subprocesses remain within this same helper group; neither helper nor descendants may detach into another group. Successful result receipt is not successful cleanup: retain group ownership and observe all live group members independently of helper-leader exit.

Apply a finite job deadline and the same asynchronous group-stop policy to this helper and all Git descendants: bounded completion wait, TERM on expiry/invalid output/abandonment, KILL within0.25s if any proven live group member remains, then at most1.0s death observation. Pipes and cleanup phases remain selector-managed; no helper join/wait/communicate or response-send may block the supervisor cancellation timer. Reap its leader separately after observed exit.

Bound and correlate every helper message. Malformed, oversized, wrong-job, stale or late messages and EOF without one complete valid result fail closed; a late success cannot overwrite a prior timeout/failure. Stage a valid result privately until complete helper-group death and current-snapshot revalidation are established. Applying the result remains exclusively the supervisor publication step; helper output never frees the runtime lane or manufactures a terminal operation.

On unresolved helper-group death or ownership ambiguity retain private unresolved-job identity, pending cleanup and infrastructure uncertainty. Refuse handoff publication, new project admission, successful close and explicit reconstruction across that unresolved lifetime; keep the controlling supervisor alive to service runtime cancellation and further bounded observation. Do not silently discard jobs, leak inherited locks/endpoints, claim closed, or carry a live old helper into a new generation. Existing running/unknown/busy runtime records remain truthful and unchanged unless an independently observed runtime event justifies their transition.
